channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: India officially permits import of pomegranates and peppers from Uzbekistan
item.description: India has officially authorized the import of pomegranates and peppers from Uzbekistan. Uzbekistan is also working to establish a "green corridor" to simplify the import of pineapples and papayas from India.

item.title: US Military AI Use Nearly Led to War with China, CNN Reports
item.description: US military personnel almost intercepted a Chinese vessel in spring 2026 based on faulty AI-generated data, CNN reported, citing four sources. The AI incorrectly identified a ship in the Middle East as carrying nuclear program components. The operation was halted after officials reviewed the AI's analysis, which was deemed "completely wrong."

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's National Electric Network tasked with strengthening power grids for winter
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's National Electric Network has been instructed to enhance preparations of its power grids for the upcoming autumn-winter period. The Ministry of Energy emphasized the importance of equipment repair, staff readiness for increased loads, and stocking necessary materials and backup power sources.

item.title: Dozens killed and injured in ongoing clashes between US and Iran
item.description: Dozens of people have been killed and injured amid ongoing exchanges of fire between the United States and Iran. The two countries continue their attacks on each other's regions.

item.title: Former Kyrgyzstan Emergency Situations Minister Boobek Ajikeev arrested pending investigation
item.description: Former Kyrgyzstan Emergency Situations Minister Boobek Ajikeev has been arrested pending investigation. The court ordered his detention until November 18. He is accused of abuse of office related to violations during the construction of a building near the Ala-Archa river.

item.title: Uzbekistan covers tuition for over 11,000 female master's students in six months
item.description: In six months, Uzbekistan has covered the tuition fees for over 11,000 female master's students. The state allocated a total of 75.5 billion UZS from the budget for these payments, a 57.3% increase compared to the previous year.

item.title: Interest Rate for Family Entrepreneurship Loans in Karakalpakstan to Decrease to 12%
item.description: The interest rate for family entrepreneurship loans in Karakalpakstan will be reduced from 17.5% to 12%. This initiative aims to support at least 30,000-40,000 more entrepreneurs. A 300 billion soum credit line at 16% will be opened for reliable customers, with the Entrepreneurship Development Company covering 4% of the interest.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Import of Russian Fertilizers Increased by Two-Thirds in First Half of 2026
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's import of Russian fertilizers surged by two-thirds in the first half of 2026. From January to June, Kyrgyzstan purchased nearly 6 million tons of fertilizers from Russia for $20.3 million. Russia's share in Kyrgyzstan's fertilizer imports rose from 40% to 50%.

item.title: Group facilitating illegal SAT exam test-taking for others apprehended in Tashkent
item.description: Authorities in Tashkent have dismantled a group, largely composed of university students, that facilitated illegal SAT certificate acquisition. The group operated a "bunker" where individuals remotely solved test questions for candidates. One member charged $1,500 per certificate, receiving payment via cryptocurrency.

item.title: Uzbekistan constructing world's largest wind power station worth $2.6 billion
item.description: Construction has begun on a 1.5 GW wind power station in northwestern Uzbekistan, a project valued at $2.6 billion in partnership with Saudi Arabia's ACWA Power. The facility will include 1,500 km of power lines and three substations. This project aims to address electricity deficits and attract investment.

item.title: US military nearly attacked Chinese ship due to AI error, CNN reports
item.description: US military personnel nearly attacked a Chinese vessel due to an artificial intelligence error, CNN reported, citing a US military intelligence analyst. The AI incorrectly concluded the ship was transporting components for Iran's nuclear program by combining open-source and classified data.

item.title: Group facilitating illegal SAT certificate acquisition exposed in Tashkent
item.description: A group in Tashkent has been exposed for illegally facilitating SAT certificate acquisition. The suspects reportedly set up a 'bunker' in a private school building to complete test questions on behalf of applicants. Further details were provided via a link to the Daryo.uz report.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Culture Ministry forms commission to investigate Bishkek Choreographic School complaints
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Culture, Information, and Youth Policy has established a commission to investigate allegations at the Bishkek Choreographic School. The commission will examine complaints from former staff and teachers regarding pressure, threats, and dismissals. Issues with the educational process and student departures were also reported.

item.title: Uzbekistan to purchase 10 Škoda electric trains for Tashkent suburban routes
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to acquire 10 Škoda 25Ev electric trains for 157 million euros to operate on Tashkent's suburban routes. The project, approved by the Tashkent City Council, is scheduled for implementation between 2026 and 2030.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan braces for flu and ARVI season starting late September
item.description: Kyrgyzstan anticipates a seasonal rise in ARVI and flu cases by late September or early October, according to the National Public Health Institute director. The health ministry urges citizens to prepare for the upcoming epidemic season.

item.title: Uzbek President tasks regional governors with developing Karakalpakstan neighborhoods
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has assigned regional governors the task of developing neighborhoods they are responsible for in Karakalpakstan. The proposal was made to name streets and neighborhoods after the regions that improved them if residents approve.

item.title: Chinese agricultural delegation explores agricultural potential in Tajikistan's Dangara district
item.description: A delegation from China's Ministry of Agriculture visited Tajikistan's Dangara district to explore agricultural potential and discuss expanding cooperation. Discussions focused on investment, modern technologies, and increasing agricultural exports between the two countries.

item.title: Karakalpakstan to become a major center for "green" energy production, says president
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced that Karakalpakstan is set to become a major hub for "green" energy production. New energy capacities totaling 860 MW have been commissioned, increasing electricity generation fourfold. Green energy's share in total production reached 23%.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's manufacturing industry output reached nearly 476 billion soms
item.description: From January to August 2026, Kyrgyzstan's manufacturing industry produced goods worth 475.966 billion soms, a 10.1% increase year-on-year. Chemical production saw the largest growth, increasing 2.3 times.

item.title: Tashkent-Nukus high-speed train service to launch in March next year
item.description: The Tashkent-Nukus high-speed train service is scheduled to commence in March of the following year. Additionally, projects worth $8 billion in artificial intelligence and data centers are planned for Qoraqalpog‘iston.

item.title: El Niño could cause new crisis in some Asian countries, study suggests
item.description: El Niño may pose a risk of a new crisis in several Asian countries, according to a study. The conflict in Iran is exacerbating the situation by negatively impacting fuel and fertilizer supplies crucial for agriculture.

item.title: High-speed Tashkent-Nukus train service to launch in March 2027
item.description: A high-speed train service between Tashkent and Nukus will commence in March 2027, reducing travel time from 16 to 7 hours. Additionally, 240 km of the A-380 highway have been fully concreted with Asian Development Bank funding. Construction has begun on another 92 km section.

item.title: Central Asia losing glaciers and water resources, WMO study finds
item.description: A World Meteorological Organization (WMO) study indicates Central Asia is experiencing reduced water resources and glacial mass. Water inflow to Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Afghanistan has significantly decreased. The region is among those with the lowest river flow, with particular concern for the Aral Sea basin.

item.title: 3.3 GW Wind Power Plants to Launch in Karakalpakstan, Aiming for 76% Green Energy by 2030
item.description: Karakalpakstan plans to launch 3.3 GW wind power plants and establish 400 MW energy storage capacity. The region aims to increase the share of "green" energy to 76% by 2030.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva: Investments in Karakalpakstan are Growing, New Significant Projects Emerging
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva stated that investments directed to Karakalpakstan are increasing, with new significant projects emerging. The visit marked the launch of major projects in energy, industry, transport, and healthcare, many in collaboration with foreign partners.

item.title: UN: Women Earn 18% Less Than Men on Average Globally
item.description: Globally, women earn 18% less than men on average, according to the International Labour Organization's Director-General Gilbert F. Houngbo. He stressed that equal work deserves equal pay and called for joint efforts to eliminate structural barriers and ensure equal pay for women.

item.title: CIS Anti-Corruption Council Holds 11th Meeting in Minsk, Tajikistan Participates
item.description: The 11th meeting of the Interstate Council for Combating Corruption of CIS member states took place in Minsk, Belarus. A delegation from Tajikistan's Agency for State Financial Control and Anti-Corruption attended. The meeting addressed issues of combating corruption, asset confiscation, and anti-corruption expertise.

item.title: Uzbekistan to build waste-to-energy plants in three regions with $395 million investment
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to construct waste-to-energy plants in Surxondaryo, Buxoro, and Qoraqalpog‘iston regions. The projects will attract $395 million in direct investment to process solid municipal waste and generate electricity. China's CSET will invest $150 million in the Surxondaryo project, aiming for 126 million kWh annually.

item.title: CSTO joint exercise 'Rubezh-2026' active phase concludes in Kazakhstan
item.description: The active phase of the joint CSTO exercise 'Rubezh-2026' involving the Central Asian Regional Collective Rapid Deployment Force (CRDF) has concluded in Kazakhstan. The drills simulated blocking and destroying illegal armed groups that had seized territory and settlements near the border.

item.title: Dushanbe hosts interdepartmental meeting on civil aviation security
item.description: An interdepartmental commission meeting on civil aviation security was held in Dushanbe, chaired by the Deputy Prime Minister. The meeting aimed to coordinate efforts to prevent and neutralize threats to passengers, crew, aircraft, and airports. Participants discussed preparations for an upcoming ICAO audit.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov arrives in the USA for a working visit
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov has arrived in the U.S. state of Utah for a working visit. He was met at the airport in Salt Lake City by Senate President Stuart Adams. Japarov will then travel to New York to attend the UN General Assembly's high-level week and hold bilateral meetings.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: New decree allows entry into civil service without competition for certain groups
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov has amended rules for forming a civil service personnel reserve. Citizens with disabilities, graduates of specific lyceums and foreign programs, and distinguished graduates of Kyrgyz universities can now enter the reserve without competition if they meet qualifications. Rules for rotation and application submission have also been clarified.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Strengthens Sanctions Control for Domestic Protection
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is enhancing its sanctions control primarily to protect its own banks, investors, and businesses, not solely to meet foreign demands. The Minister of Economy stated the goal is to maintain economic activity within legal frameworks, avoid sanctions circumvention, and protect financial institutions from secondary sanctions risks.

item.title: New modern building material production expands in Karakalpakstan
item.description: A new enterprise, "Coals KS," in Nukus, Karakalpakstan, is expanding its production of modern building materials like gas blocks and lime. The $16.3 million project utilizes local raw materials and aims to supply both domestic and export markets, including Kazakhstan and Turkmenistan. The facility currently employs 200 local residents.

item.title: Modern thermal insulation materials produced in Nukus from local basalt
item.description: The "Nukus Insulation Group" enterprise in Nukus, Karakalpakstan, is producing modern thermal insulation materials from local basalt. The $50 million project, equipped with European technology, can produce 50,000 tons annually, meeting international standards. It creates 150 new jobs and enhances building energy efficiency.

item.title: Tashkent Metro undergoes significant expansion and modernization over the past decade
item.description: The Tashkent Metro has seen substantial development, adding 33 kilometers of new lines and 21 stations in recent years, expanding its network to 71 kilometers and 50 stations. Modernization efforts include new trains, digital payment systems, and improved safety and convenience for over a million daily passengers.

item.title: Tashkent Real Estate Fraud: Izmir Art Stroy Head Arrested, New Company to Continue Construction
item.description: Tashkent authorities have arrested the head of Izmir Art Stroy LLC amid an investigation into alleged fraud. The company is accused of taking over 287 billion soums from 1,530 citizens for apartments in unfinished housing complexes. A new company will now complete the construction projects.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Russia Sign Cooperation Program to Combat Corruption
item.description: Uzbekistan and Russia have approved a cooperation program to combat corruption for 2027-2028. The agreement, signed by the Prosecutor General of Russia and the Director of Uzbekistan's Anti-Corruption Agency, includes exchanging experience, implementing digital tools for risk identification, developing anti-corruption culture, and fostering scientific and educational collaboration.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan Discuss Migration Issues
item.description: The Ambassador of Kyrgyzstan to Kazakhstan, Kudaybergen Bazarbaev, met with the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Kazakhstan, Mukhtar Tileuberdi, to discuss bilateral cooperation. Key topics included implementing tasks set by the heads of state to elevate relations and creating favorable conditions for the stay, transit, and employment of citizens from both countries.

item.title: South Korea's Pragmatic Partnership Strengths in Central Asia Highlighted by Experts
item.description: Experts note South Korea's key advantage in Central Asia lies in its blend of technological capacity, investment potential, and practical modernization experience. Unlike many external players, South Korea's own economic development journey makes its expertise highly relevant for Central Asian nations seeking diversification and industrial growth. Its ability to adapt solutions to specific needs and its perceived neutral, pragmatic stance are significant strengths.
